profiles.summary: The endpoint in networks.json still runs reth v2.11.0, which pins evm2 at commit 66687c18 and ruint 1.21.1, and every vector, script and mined swap rerun this cycle matches. New: the released reth binary carries the evm2 LLVM compiler as a default feature, and a node started with --jit runs it for block building and payload validation while eth_call never does. Public mainnet endpoints now span four interpreter generations, and the newest geth dispatch code is on no public endpoint found.

deltas.delta: reth v2.11.0 builds with the features jit, gmp, asm-keccak and keccak-cache-global by default (bin/reth/Cargo.toml lines 89-100). The jit feature links evm2-jit with its LLVM backend at the same evm2 revision 66687c18 (Cargo.toml line 439, crates/ethereum/evm/Cargo.toml lines 23 and 66-71). It is switched off at run time unless the operator passes --jit (crates/node/core/src/args/jit.rs line 12, default false).

When --jit is on, the payload builder (crates/ethereum/payload/src/lib.rs line 205) and the engine's payload validation (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs line 1033) call with_jit_support, which installs the JIT interpreter runner (crates/ethereum/evm/src/factory.rs lines 456-470). The eth_call helper (crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/helpers/call.rs) has no JIT reference. A contract is compiled after 8 lookups, and the default bytecode length limit is 0, meaning no limit (jit.rs lines 69-73), so the 24,009 byte PoolManager is eligible. The node logs the backend as experimental.

reth replaced revm with evm2 as its EVM in v2.9.0 of 29 October 2026. v2.10.0 (5 November) pinned evm2 592bf18, and v2.10.1 and v2.11.0 (11 November) followed with performance and stability changes. No release note between v2.9.0 and v2.11.0 names an opcode result fix. The evm2 path on mainnet reth nodes is therefore about four weeks old.

Public Ethereum endpoints answer with geth v1.16.7 built with go1.25.14 (1rpc.io and eth.rpc.blxrbdn.com), reth v2.10.0 on evm2 (eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io), reth v2.7.0 and v2.6.0 on revm (eth-pokt.nodies.app and rpc.flashbots.net), and reth v2.11.0 (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com), by web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24. No public endpoint found runs geth v1.17.9 or v1.17.10.

geth v1.17.9 (21 October 2026) made opcode dispatch an inlined switch, and v1.17.10 (23 October) merged PR 35959, which folds DUP1 to DUP16 and SWAP1 to SWAP16 into one case each and moves the next opcode fetch to the end of each case. The PR describes no change of semantics or stack bounds. v1.17.8 hardened jump destination analysis caching for attack cases after Amsterdam.
crates.io lists ruint 1.21.1 of 23 October 2026 as the newest release, with 1.21.0 yanked. There is no later fix to read.

profiles.summary: No new state-model difference is live. Glamsterdam, which has no mainnet date, brings block-level access lists and clients that execute a block's transactions in parallel driven by them, and geth has already fixed one fault in that code. Transient storage stays scoped to one transaction under it.

deltas.delta: The Glamsterdam meta EIP lists Sepolia at 2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC and leaves Hoodi and Mainnet empty. It includes EIP-7928 (block-level access lists) and EIP-7732 (enshrined proposer-builder separation).

geth v1.17.6 implements parallel block execution driven by the block-level access list. v1.17.9 fixes an RPC call made at the same time as block processing that could corrupt the access list, and v1.17.10 postpones the Hoodi activation with no new date.

profiles.summary: ETH remains the only gas asset. The Glamsterdam gas EIPs change costs and block accounting but not what a call returns to the PoolManager, apart from the out-of-gas cases cycle 8 already cleared. EIP-7708 adds a log for every ETH transfer and does not change balances.

deltas.delta: Glamsterdam includes EIP-2780 (resource based intrinsic gas), EIP-7778 (block gas accounting without refunds), EIP-7976 and EIP-7981 (calldata floor and access list cost), EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 (state creation and state access gas) and EIP-7708 (ETH transfers emit a log).

profiles.summary: No new system contract or precompile is live. Glamsterdam's deterministic factory names the address where the 69 byte CREATE2 factory already lives on mainnet, and the GMP library that reth now links is used only by the MODEXP precompile.

deltas.delta: EIP-7997 requires the CREATE2 wrapper bytecode at 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C, passes the call value to the created contract, and returns the new address or reverts with empty data.

The gmp feature of evm2 at 66687c18 switches only the MODEXP precompile to GMP (crates/evm2/src/precompiles/modexp.rs lines 9 and 53-70, precompiles/mod.rs lines 76-77). The opcode arithmetic still goes through ruint.

findings.title: The released reth binary carries an LLVM compiler for EVM code that validates and builds Ethereum blocks when an operator enables it, and no simulated call can reach it
findings.difference: reth v2.11.0, the client behind the endpoint in networks.json, links the evm2 JIT and its LLVM backend by default. With --jit, a contract that has been looked up 8 times is compiled to native code with no size limit, and that native code then runs inside payload building and payload validation. eth_call, eth_estimateGas and debug_traceCall run the interpreter. On Ethereum a block is accepted only if the execution clients of a supermajority of validators agree, and reth is a small minority client on every published census.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager is called in many blocks, so on a reth node with --jit it becomes resident compiled code within minutes. From then on every swap that node executes runs FullMath.mulDiv (MULMOD with modulus 2^256 - 1 and with the pool denominator), the SAR and SIGNEXTEND unpacking of Slot0 and BalanceDelta, the BYTE and shift lookups of BitMath and the signed division of TickBitmap.compress in code generated by LLVM. If that code computed one of these differently, the reth node would compute a different post-state root for the block. As a builder it would publish a block that geth, Nethermind, Besu and Erigon reject. As a validator it would reject the canonical block and fall off the chain. Neither outcome changes the balances that the canonical chain records for LPs, swappers or claim holders, because the majority clients decide the canonical state. An ordinary account cannot switch the compiler on, cannot choose which node builds its block, and gains nothing from a divergence on a minority client. The vectors, scripts and mined swap checks of this review never reach this path: simulated calls do not use it, and mined swaps are the output of whichever client built the block, which was rechecked here against the source on 30,321 swaps of blocks 26,485,859 to 26,487,858 without a mismatch.
findings.impact: No loss to users of the canonical chain. A reth operator who enables --jit risks missed slots or rejected blocks if the compiler is wrong. Only if reth with --jit came to build and attest for a supermajority could a compiler fault reach canonical pool state.
findings.preconditions: A node operator starts reth v2.11.0 or later with --jit, and the generated code for one of the opcodes above differs from the specification for an input the pool math produces.
findings.mitigations: Track client share and the --jit flag in reth releases. Before relying on reth block production, read or test the JIT code generation for MULMOD, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SDIV and SMOD, as was done for Monad. The deployer needs no change to the PoolManager.

sources.supports: jit and gmp are default features of the reth binary (lines 89-104)
--jit defaults to false, hot threshold 8, max bytecode length 0 meaning no limit
payload validation calls with_jit_support (line 1033) and can use resident compiled code (lines 233-238)
the JIT runner is installed only when jit_support is set (lines 376-386, 456-470)
the node logs the backend as experimental (line 565) and builds the executor through build_evm_config (lines 606-610)
reth is listed at 3 to 7.67 percent of execution clients; the page marks its data as stale
web3_clientVersion returns reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc and rpc_modules lists no JIT namespace

cleared.check: Rerun of battery.py (99,985 vectors) and targeted.py (85,544 vectors, among them 24,154 MULMOD and 21,074 512 bit mulDiv inputs) on the reth v2.11.0 endpoint in networks.json on 2026-11-24.
cleared.result: All 185,529 vectors returned the specified word, with no error. The evm2 and ruint 1.21.1 paths are unchanged since the last run.

cleared.check: Rerun of pmdiff.py (250 scripts) and pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) with the deployed PoolManager bytecode on the reth v2.11.0 endpoint.
cleared.result: The reference record is the one OPCODES.md gives: 11,892 calls with 11,225 successes and 667 reverts for the first set, and 15,886 calls with 14,622 successes and 1,264 failures for the second, with the same revert selectors. The bytecode hash after the immutable rewrite is a7aaa3ba6ae795c3.

cleared.check: swaps.py over the newest mined Swap events of the Ethereum PoolManager (blocks 26,485,859 to 26,487,858) and replay.py of the multi-step and unexplained samples.
cleared.result: 30,321 swaps: 30,318 satisfy the tick relation exactly and 3 sit on a tick boundary as Pool.swap leaves them (src/libraries/Pool.sol:430-431), none mismatches. Of 27,246 pairs, 25,446 match one step of SwapMath.computeSwapStep. All 34 sampled multi-step and other swaps replay to the unit through the swap loop, the longest with 91 steps.

cleared.check: The opcode battery and the targeted set on two other Ethereum mainnet clients behind public endpoints: geth v1.16.7 (eth.rpc.blxrbdn.com, holiman uint256 arithmetic) and reth v2.10.0 on evm2 revision 592bf18 (eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io).
cleared.result: Both returned the specified word for all 99,985 battery vectors and all 85,544 targeted vectors with no error, so the geth family and the previous evm2 revision agree with the specification on the same edges, including the MULMOD inputs built for the ruint 1.21.0 fault.

cleared.check: pmdiff.py, 250 scripts with the deployed PoolManager bytecode under identical state, run on geth v1.16.7 (eth.rpc.blxrbdn.com) and reth v2.10.0 on evm2 (eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io) against the reth v2.11.0 reference.
cleared.result: Both clients returned records identical to the reference for 250 of 250 scripts with no error. The pool math, liquidity, swap, donate, claim and settlement paths compute the same bytes on the geth interpreter, the previous evm2 revision and the current one.

cleared.check: Do the opcodes that Glamsterdam defines (SLOTNUM 0x4b of EIP-7843, DUPN 0xe6, SWAPN 0xe7 and EXCHANGE 0xe8 of EIP-8024) change how the existing PoolManager bytecode decodes or where it may jump?
cleared.result: A linear decode of the 24,009 byte deployed code and of the build of this checkout finds none of these bytes, nor 0x1e, 0x49 or 0x4a, at an instruction boundary, and 610 jump destinations in both. EIP-8024 also keeps jump destination analysis unchanged by making 0x5b an invalid immediate. The code therefore decodes and jumps the same after the fork.

cleared.check: EIP-8246 stops SELFDESTRUCT from burning ETH in the same-transaction self-beneficiary case and keeps the balance of accounts it clears. Could forced or retained ETH become a credit at the PoolManager?
cleared.result: Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), and sync for the native currency only resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283). A balance that arrives without a call is never credited to anyone, before or after the fork. The PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT.

cleared.check: EIP-7997 deterministic factory as a new predeploy that the PoolManager could meet as recipient, currency or hook.
cleared.result: The address 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C already holds the 69 byte CREATE2 factory on Ethereum, which cycle 8 swept with 18 call shapes. The EIP passes the call value to the created contract and otherwise reverts, so nothing new reaches the PoolManager.

cleared.check: Does the GMP library that the reth v2.11.0 binary links by default touch opcode arithmetic?
cleared.result: In evm2 66687c18 the gmp feature replaces only the MODEXP precompile implementation (precompiles/modexp.rs lines 53-70). The PoolManager never calls MODEXP except where a caller names 0x05 as its own currency or recipient.

cleared.check: Is there a ruint release after 1.21.1 or a reth release after v2.11.0 that changes an arithmetic path the PoolManager uses?
cleared.result: crates.io lists 1.21.1 of 23 October 2026 as newest, and the reth release page lists v2.11.0 of 11 November as newest. The reth v2.11.0 lock file pins ruint 1.21.1 and evm2 66687c18, the pair OPCODES.md already records as read.

leads.question: Does the evm2 JIT at revision 66687c18 generate MULMOD, ADDMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SAR, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE code that matches the specification, in particular MULMOD with the modulus 2^256 - 1 and with the constant moduli 2^96 and 2^128 that the PoolManager bytecode uses?
leads.why: A reth node with --jit validates and builds blocks with this code and no simulated call reaches it. A fault there is operator level while reth is a minority, and it would matter more if reth share or JIT adoption grows.

leads.question: Rerun battery.py, targeted.py and pmdiff.py on a geth v1.17.9 or v1.17.10 node once a public endpoint serves one, since the inlined dispatch and the merged DUP and SWAP cases are on no endpoint found today.
leads.why: geth is the largest execution client, and its dispatch loop was rewritten twice in October 2026. The PR text describes no change of semantics, which was not tested.

leads.question: When Glamsterdam gets a mainnet date, do the parallel executors driven by block-level access lists in geth and reth keep each transaction's transient storage and the PoolManager's storage writes in transaction order for blocks with many PoolManager transactions?
leads.why: geth already fixed one fault in this code (v1.17.9). A parallel execution fault in a supermajority client could change what the canonical state records for pools touched by several transactions in one block.
